title: Oozing Charred Chinese Katsuobushi Wonton Soup
description: A briny, creamy wonton soup with charred katsuobushi garnishes, perfect for a solo, flexitarian dinner.
instructions: In a large pot over medium, combine chicken broth, coconut milk, soy sauce, mirin, sesame oil, grated ginger, and minced garlic, bringing to a gentle boil.
Add sliced shiitake mushrooms and simmer for 5 minutes until softened.
While the broth simmers, mix ground tofu, a pinch of salt, and 1 tsp katsuobushi flakes to create the filling.
Place about 1 tsp of filling in the center of each wonton wrapper, fold into triangles, seal edges with water, and set aside.
Heat a nonstick skillet over high heat and quickly char each wonton for 30 seconds on each side, giving them a smoky char.
Gently drop the charred wontons into the simmering broth and cook until they float and the wrappers are translucent, about 4 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low, stir in seaweed flakes for a briny finish, and swirl in a splash of coconut milk for creaminess.
Ladle soup into bowls, garnish with chopped scallions and additional katsuobushi flakes, and serve hot.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
